proof.criterion: Review round 1's Important finding: e2e-local.sh must refuse a second run in the same checkout before it removes anything, so a running first run keeps its store, logs and evidence.
proof.surface: The script itself, two runs at once in this one checkout, and the driver's own test suite.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy && bash scripts/e2e-local.test.sh ; and by hand: bash scripts/e2e-local.sh & then (once run 1 is up) E2E_NATS_PORT=14422 E2E_PORT=19220 E2E_SESSION_PORT=19221 bash scripts/e2e-local.sh ; with ls -1 out/e2e before and after
proof.observed: All four cases of e2e-local.test.sh pass, the new one 'PASS: refuses a second run in the same checkout, and the first finishes with its evidence'. By hand: run 2 exits 3 with 'ERR: another run of e2e-local.sh is using <workspace>/packages/envoy/out/e2e; this run removed nothing.', the ls -1 out/e2e listings before and after it are identical, and run 1 then prints its own PASS and exits 0 with envelopes.jsonl at 13,980 bytes and listener.log present. The mechanism: the script takes an exclusive flock on out/e2e/run.lock between mkdir -p out/e2e and everything destructive, and arms the EXIT trap only once it holds it, so the refusal is ahead of the destruction rather than behind it; flock joins the prerequisite command list. The shell holds the lock for its own life, so it needs no cleanup, and run.lock is in neither rm list and is a sibling of nats-store rather than inside it.
proof.negativeControl: The new case run against the reviewed script, restored from 2c75d9b561a4 at the same path and put back afterwards: it fails with 'FAIL: the second run did not say that another run holds <dir>', the second run having cleared the first's directory. With the fix it passes.

trickyParts: ReloadOptions refuses an Options whose Port or HTTPPort differs from the one the server was started with ('config reload not supported for HTTPPort: old=-1, new=52544'). Server.Reload therefore builds the new Options from the new configuration text and then restores Host, Port, HTTPPort, HTTPHost, StoreDir, NoSigs, ConfigFile and the JetStream flag from the options the server was started with, and never reads a port back from the running server. TestARefusedReloadAnswersWithTheServersReasonAndKeepsTheOldConfiguration pins it.

natsserver.ConfigureOptions leaves its parse in natsserver.FlagSnapshot, a package-level variable every later ReloadOptions in the process merges over the options it is given, whatever server they belong to. serverOptions clears it under a package flagsMu that Reload takes too, so one test binary's several servers never read each other's command line.
